decisions.reason: The XL package of the anamnesis app extends an established, in-house developed product to larger practices, so the firm fully understands and can refine it at minimal cost.
Support for dental assistants draws directly on the firm's core service and training know-how, so the firm can absorb user feedback and keep improving the service instead of withdrawing it.

The materials management module builds on the firm's deep knowledge of practice workflows and its in-house development, but it is only mentioned on the website, so the firm should keep it while using early adoption feedback to judge its value.

The KIM secure messaging service is tied to mandatory telematics infrastructure that the firm already masters, and its ongoing regulatory updates show continued investment, making withdrawal very unlikely.
